Avogadro guide · Minecraft 1.12.2 / Cleanroom

Two fictional atom examples

Give a fictional element the atom details you want players to inspect. The two examples define Naquadah with electrons and with every electron removed; you supply the counts and positions rather than asking Avogadro to predict them.

Example language Your choice applies across the guides.
Java imports 
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.*;
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.molecule.*;
// Client code only:
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*;
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.client.export.*;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

Naquadah: an invented neutral atom

This example defines an invented neutral naquadah atom with 174 protons. The supplied neutron count and electron shells determine the inspection display. Register the returned definition to make it available in game; these values are game data, not a prediction that this nucleus is stable.

Java · add this method to your class.

public static MoleculeSpec fictionalNaquadah() {
    // Fictional nucleus and chosen shell layout, not a prediction of a real element.
    return AvogadroApi.builder("guide:naquadah")
        .name("Naquadah (fictional)")
        .atom("Nq", 0, 0, 0)
        .noBonds()
        .element("Nq", 174, 352, 2, 8, 18, 32, 50, 32, 18, 14)
        .build();
}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described. 

static MoleculeSpec fictionalNaquadah() {
    // Fictional nucleus and chosen shell layout, not a prediction of a real element.
    return AvogadroApi.builder("guide:naquadah")
        .name("Naquadah (fictional)")
        .atom("Nq", 0, 0, 0)
        .noBonds()
        .element("Nq", 174, 352, 2, 8, 18, 32, 50, 32, 18, 14)
        .build();
}

JSON · one definition per file unless a different destination is shown. 

{
  "name": "Naquadah (fictional)",
  "atoms": [
    {
      "e": "Nq",
      "x": 0,
      "y": 0,
      "z": 0
    }
  ],
  "bonds": [],
  "elements": {
    "Nq": {
      "atomic_number": 174,
      "neutrons": 352,
      "electron_shells": [
        2,
        8,
        18,
        32,
        50,
        32,
        18,
        14
      ]
    }
  }
}

The chosen shell counts sum to 174 and satisfy the API’s count limits. That validates the data format, not whether such an atom could exist. There is no standard atomic weight for Nq; do not advertise a standard-weight molecular mass.

The same fictional nucleus with every electron removed

This keeps the fictional nucleus but removes every electron by setting charge to +174 and supplying no occupied shells. It tests how the atom viewer handles a bare nucleus; it does not calculate the energy required to remove those electrons.

Java · add this method to your class.

public static MoleculeSpec fictionalStrippedIon() {
    // Same fictional nucleus with no electrons: an illustration of explicit ion data.
    return AvogadroApi.builder("guide:naquadah_nucleus")
        .name("Bare naquadah nucleus (fictional)")
        .atom("Nq", 0, 0, 0)
        .noBonds()
        .atomConfiguration(0, 174, 352, 174)
        .build();
}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described. 

static MoleculeSpec fictionalStrippedIon() {
    // Same fictional nucleus with no electrons: an illustration of explicit ion data.
    return AvogadroApi.builder("guide:naquadah_nucleus")
        .name("Bare naquadah nucleus (fictional)")
        .atom("Nq", 0, 0, 0)
        .noBonds()
        .atomConfiguration(0, 174, 352, 174)
        .build();
}

JSON · one definition per file unless a different destination is shown. 

{
  "name": "Bare naquadah nucleus (fictional)",
  "atoms": [
    {
      "e": "Nq",
      "x": 0,
      "y": 0,
      "z": 0
    }
  ],
  "bonds": [],
  "atom_configurations": {
    "0": {
      "atomic_number": 174,
      "neutrons": 352,
      "charge": 174,
      "electron_shells": []
    }
  }
}

A charge of +174 and no shell entries explicitly gives zero electrons. This demonstrates a nucleus-only inspection case. Stability, energy, radiation, and material properties are outside this rendering API.

Calls used in the examples

Calls used in this guide
Call or setting Arguments What it does
atom(symbol, x, y, z) Fictional symbol; position Place the atom in your model.
noBonds() No arguments Declare a model with no bonds.
element(symbol, protons, mass, shells...) Symbol; nuclear data; electron shells Describe the fictional element used by this definition.
build() No arguments Return the definition; register it separately to make it available in game.

When you finish: A builder creates a model but does not add it to the game. Java registrations use a name, called an owner, to group the definitions your mod controls; choose your mod ID. A RegistrationJob lets you cancel pending work or remove its installed set later. JSON and Groovy registrations use their file or script loading rules instead. Keep drawing and exports in client code.
